L97: # Highway Performance Monitoring System Field Manual
L98: 
L99: ## Chapter 4 Data Requirements and Specifications
L100: 
L101: ### (cont)
L102: #### Item 3: Facility_Type (Facility Type)
L103: 
L104: Description: The operational characteristic of the roadway.
L105: 
L106: Use: For determining public road mileage, for investment requirements modeling to calculate capacity and estimate roadway deficiencies and improvement needs, in the cost allocation pavement model, and in the national highway database; for the querying and analysis of data (e.g., transportation performance management (TPM) metrics, Federal-aid project information, etc.) by facility type.
L107: Extent: All Public highways including ramps located within grade-separated interchanges as identified in 23 U.S.C 101.a(27).
L108: 
L109: Functional System  |  | 1  | 2  | 3  | 4  | 5  | 6  | 7
L110: --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | ---
L111: NHS  | IH  | OFE  | OPA  | MiA  | MaC  | MiC  | Local
L112: --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | ---
L113: Rural  | FE+R  | FE+R  | FE+R  | FE+R  | FE+R  | FE+R  | FE+R  | FE+R
L114: Urban  | FE+R  | FE+R  | FE+R  | FE+R  | FE+R  | FE+R  | FE+R  | FE+R
L115: FE + R = Full Extent & Ramps
L116: Coding Requirements for Fields 8, 9, and 10:
L117: 
L118: Value_Numeric: Use one of the following codes as applicable regardless of whether or not the section is on a structure. The definition for each code is as follows:
L119: Code  | Description
L120: --- | ---
L121: 1  | One-Way Roadway  | Roadway that operates with traffic moving in a single direction during non-peak period hours.
L122: 2  | Two-Way Roadway  | Roadway that operates with traffic moving in both directions during non-peak period hours.
L123: 4  | Ramp  | Non-mainline junction or connector facility contained within a grade-separated interchange.
L124: 5  | Non Mainline  | All non-mainline facilities excluding ramps.
L125: 6  | Non Inventory Direction  | Individual road/roads of a multi-road facility that is/are not used for determining the primary length for the facility.
L126: 7  | Planned/Unbuilt  | Planned roadway that has yet to be constructed.
L127: Value_Text: No entry required. Available for State Use.
L128: 
L129: Value_Date: No entry required. Available for State Use.
L130: 
L131: Guidance: General
L132: 
L133: Public road mileage is based only on sections coded ‘1,’ or ‘2’. This includes only those roads that are open to public travel regardless of the ownership or maintenance responsibilities. Ramps are not included in the public road mileage calculation.
L134: Frontage roads and service roads that are public roads shall be coded either as one-way (Code ‘1’) or two-way (Code ‘2’) roadways.
L135: 
L136: Use Code ‘7’ to identify a new roadway section that has been approved per the State Transportation Improvement Plan (STIP), but has yet to be built.
L137: 
L138: ”One-way Pairs” (See Figure 4.5)
L139: 
L140: Characteristics:
L141:   * Divided roadway sections that have the same route designation (e.g., Route 1), but different street names (e.g., West Avenue, and East Avenue);
L142:   * Typically located in an urban area or a city/town;
L143:   * Usually connects to roadways with two-way traffic;
L144:   * Are typically separated by some physical or visual element other than a curb or barrier, such as buildings, landscaping, or terrain;
L145:   * Parallel roadway sections which complement each other in providing access at both termini; and
L146:   * Not designated as an Interstate
L147: Ramps
L148: 
L149: Ramps may consist of directional connectors from either an Interstate to another Interstate, or from an Interstate to a different functional system. Moreover, ramps allow ingress and egress to grade separated highways. Ramps may consist of traditional ramps, acceleration and deceleration lanes, as well as collector-distributor lanes.
L150: Ramps shall be coded with the highest order functional system within the interchange that it functions. A mainline facility that terminates at the junction with another mainline facility is not a ramp and shall be coded ‘1.’
L151: 
L152: Non-Mainlines
L153: Non-mainline facilities include roads or lanes that provide access to and from sites that are adjacent to a roadway section such as bus terminals, park and ride lots, and rest areas. These may include: special bus lanes, limited access truck roads, ramps to truck weigh stations, or a turn-around.
L154: For LRS purposes, this Data Item shall be reported independently for both directions of travel associated with divided highway sections, for which dual carriageway GIS network representation is required per guidance in Chapter 3, Section 3.3 and Table 3.5.

L191: #### Item 4: Structure_Type (Structure Type)
L192: 
L193: Description: Roadway section that is a bridge, tunnel or causeway.
L194: 
L195: Use: For analysis in the national highway database and pavement performance analysis/reporting
L196: 
L197: Extent: All Federal-aid highways.
L198: Functional System  |  | 1  | 2  | 3  | 4  | 5  | 6  | 7
L199: --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | ---
L200: NHS  | IH  | OFE  | OPA  | MiA  | MaC  | MiC  | Local
L201: --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | ---
L202: Rural  | FE**  | FE**  | FE**  | FE**  | FE**  | FE**  |  |
L203: Urban  | FE**  | FE**  | FE**  | FE**  | FE**  | FE**  | FE**  |
L204: FE** = Full Extent wherever data item is applicable
L205: 
L206: Coding Requirements for Fields 8, 9, and 10:
L207: 
L208: Value_Numeric: Use the following codes:
L209: Code  | Description
L210: --- | ---
L211: 1  | Section is a Bridge
L212: 2  | Section is a Tunnel
L213: 3  | Section is a Causeway
L214: 
L215: Value_Text: No entry required. Available for State Use.
L216: 
L217: Value_Date: No entry required. Available for State Use.
L218: 
L219: Guidance: Code this data item wherever a bridge, tunnel, or causeway exists.
L220: Bridges shall meet a minimum length requirement of more than 20 feet (per the National Bridge Inventory (NBI) guidelines in accordance with 23 CFR 650.305) in order to be deemed a “structure.” Per NBI guidelines, bridge-sized culverts shall be reported for this data item; all other culverts are to be excluded.
L221: 
L222: A tunnel is a roadway below the surface connecting to at-grade adjacent sections.
L223: A causeway is a narrow, low-lying raised roadway, usually providing a passageway over some type of vehicular travel impediment (e.g. a river, swamp, earth dam, wetlands, etc.).
L224: 
L225: In accordance with 23 CFR 490.309(c), this data shall be collected and reported on an annual cycle for the Interstate roadways and on a 2-year maximum cycle for all other required sections.
L226: The begin and end points for this data item shall be coded in accordance with the points of origin and terminus for the associated bridge, tunnel or causeway. Furthermore, the points of origin and terminus for structures shall exclude approach slabs.
L227: For LRS purposes, this Data Item can be reported independently for both directions of travel associated with divided highway sections, for which dual carriageway GIS network representation is required per guidance in Chapter 3, Section 3.3 and Table 3.5.
L228: NOTE: This data item is required to be reported for both the inventory and non-inventory directional approaches associated with all divided Interstate roadway sections where the following pavement data items have been reported in the same manner (as specified in the Metadata; see Chapter 3, Sec. 3.3, Tables 3.18 and 3.19):
L229:   * Data Item 47 (IRI)
L230:   * Data Item 48 (PSR)
L231:   * Data Item 49 (Surface Type)
L232:   * Data Item 50 (Rutting)
L233:   * Data Item 51 (Faulting)
L234:   * Data Item 52 (Cracking Percent)

L252: #### Item 5: Access_Control (Access Control)
L253: 
L254: Description: The degree of access control for a given section of road.
L255: 
L256: Use: For investment requirements modeling to calculate capacity and estimate type of design, in truck size and weight studies, and for national highway database purposes.
L257: 
L258: Extent: All principal arterials and Sample Panel sections; optional for other non-principal arterial sections beyond the limits of the Sample Panel.
L259: Functional System  |  | 1  | 2  | 3  | 4  | 5  | 6  | 7
L260: --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | ---
L261: NHS  | IH  | OFE  | OPA  | MiA  | MaC  | MiC  | Local
L262: --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | ---
L263: Rural  | FE  | FE  | FE  | FE  | SP  | SP  |  |
L264: Urban  | FE  | FE  | FE  | FE  | SP  | SP  | SP  |
L265: FE = Full Extent SP = Sample Panel Sections
L266: 
L267: Coding Requirements for Fields 8, 9, and 10:
L268: 
L269: Value_Numeric: Use the following codes:
L270: Code  | Description
L271: --- | ---
L272: 1  | Full Access Control  | Preference given to through traffic movements by providing interchanges with selected public roads, and by prohibiting crossing at-grade and direct driveway connections (i.e., limited access to the facility).
L273: 2  | Partial Access Control  | Preference given to through traffic movement. In addition to interchanges, there may be some crossings at-grade with public roads, but, direct private driveway connections have been minimized through the use of frontage roads or other local access restrictions. Control of curb cuts is not access control.
L274: 3  | No Access Control  | No degree of access control exists (i.e., full access to the facility is permitted).
L275: Value_Text: No entry required. Available for State Use.
L276: 
L277: Value_Date: No entry required. Available for State Use.
L278:

L296: #### Item 6: Ownership (Ownership)
L297: 
L298: Description: The entity that has legal ownership of a roadway.
L299: 
L300: Use: For apportionment, administrative, legislative, analytical, and national highway database purposes, and in cost allocation studies; for the querying and analysis of data (e.g., transportation performance management (TPM) metrics, Federal-aid project information, etc.) by ownership.
L301: 
L302: Extent: All Public highways as identified in 23 U.S.C 101.a(27).
L303: Functional System  |  | 1  | 2  | 3  | 4  | 5  | 6  | 7
L304: --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | ---
L305: NHS  | IH  | OFE  | OPA  | MiA  | MaC  | MiC  | Local
L306: --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | ---
L307: Rural  | FE  | FE  | FE  | FE  | FE  | FE  | FE  | FE
L308: Urban  | FE  | FE  | FE  | FE  | FE  | FE  | FE  | FE
L309: FE = Full Extent SP = Sample Panel Sections
L310: 
L311: Coding Requirements for Fields 8, 9, and 10:
L312: Value_Numeric: Code the level of government that best represents the highway owner irrespective of whether agreements exist for maintenance or other purposes. If more than one code applies, code the lowest numerical value using the following codes:
L313: Code  | Description  | Code  | Description
L314: --- | --- | --- | ---
L315: 1  | State Highway Agency  | 60  | Other Federal Agency
L316: 2  | County Highway Agency  | 62  | Bureau of Indian Affairs
L317: 3  | Town or Township Highway Agency  | 63  | Bureau of Fish and Wildlife
L318: 4  | City or Municipal Highway Agency  | 64  | U.S. Forest Service
L319: 11  | State Park, Forest, or Reservation Agency  | 66  | National Park Service
L320: 12  | Local Park, Forest or Reservation Agency  | 67  | Tennessee Valley Authority
L321: 21  | Other State Agency  | 68  | Bureau of Land Management
L322: 25  | Other Local Agency  | 69  | Bureau of Reclamation
L323: 26  | Private (other than Railroad)  | 70  | Corps of Engineers
L324: 27  | Railroad  | 72  | Air Force
L325: 31  | State Toll Road  | 73  | Navy/Marines
L326: 32  | Local Toll Authority  | 74  | Army
L327: 40  | Other Public Instrumentality (i.e., Airport)  | 80  | Other
L328: 50  | Indian Tribe Nation  |  |
L329: Value_Text: Optional. Code secondary ownership information, if applicable.
L330: 
L331: Value_Date: No entry required. Available for State Use.
L332: 
L333: Guidance: “State” means owned by one of the 50 States, the District of Columbia, or the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico including quasi-official State commissions or organizations;
L334: 
L335: “County, local, municipal, town, or township” means owned by one of the officially recognized governments established under State authority;
L336: “Federal” means owned by one of the branches of the U.S. Government or independent establishments, government corporations, quasi-official agencies, organizations, or instrumentalities;
L337: 
L338: “Other” means any other group not already described above or nongovernmental organizations with the authority to build, operate, or maintain toll or free highway facilities.
L339: 
L340: Only private roads that are open to public travel (e.g., toll bridges) are to be reported in HPMS.
L341: In cases where ownership responsibilities are shared between multiple entities, this item shall be coded based on the primary owner (i.e., the entity that has the larger degree of ownership), if applicable. Information on additional owners shall be entered in Data Field 9 for this item.
L342: For LRS purposes, this Data Item shall be reported independently for both directions of travel associated with divided highway sections, for which dual carriageway GIS network representation is required per guidance in Chapter 3, Section 3.3 and Table 3.5.
L343: #### Item 7: Through_Lanes (Through Lanes)
L344: 
L345: Description The number of lanes designated for through-traffic.
L346: 
L347: Use: For apportionment, administrative, legislative, analytical, pavement performance analysis/reporting and national highway database purposes.
L348: 
L349: Extent: All Federal-aid highways including ramps located within grade-separated interchanges.
L350: Functional System  |  | 1  | 2  | 3  | 4  | 5  | 6  | 7
L351: --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | ---
L352: NHS  | IH  | OFE  | OPA  | MiA  | MaC  | MiC  | Local
L353: --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | ---
L354: Rural  | FE+R  | FE+R  | FE+R  | FE+R  | FE+R  | FE+R  |  |
L355: Urban  | FE+R  | FE+R  | FE+R  | FE+R  | FE+R  | FE+R  | FE+R  |
L356: FE = Full Extent & Ramps
L357: 
L358: Coding Requirements for Fields 8, 9, and 10:
L359: Value_Numeric: Enter the number of through lanes in both directions carrying through traffic in the off-peak period.
L360: 
L361: Value_Text: No entry required. Available for State Use.
L362: 
L363: Value_Date: No entry required. Available for State Use.
L364: 
L365: Guidance: This Data Item shall also be reported for all ramp sections contained within grade separated interchanges.
L366: Code the number of through lanes according to the striping, if present, on multilane facilities, or according to traffic use or State/local design guidelines if no striping or only centerline striping is present.
L367: 
L368: For one-way roadways, two-way roadways, and couplets, exclude all ramps and sections defined as auxiliary lanes, such as:
L369:   * Collector-distributor lanes
L370:   * Weaving lanes
